main_topics.reason: Opening complaint; user describes urgency affecting kids and job and asks how to cope in the meantime.
Several turns on options beyond mesalamine tablets, including rectal treatment which the user had not heard of.
User has not seen a gastroenterologist since diagnosis and asks how to get seen faster given long waits.
User asked a follow-up question about calprotectin and whether it can show inflammation without a colonoscopy.
User opens with embarrassment, fears sounding stupid, and ends saying they came in ashamed.
User said it made them angry to have suffered two years believing it was normal.
User asked for practical ways to cope, especially fear of urgency during meetings.
User was told UC is just like this, felt they were complaining too much, and wants to prepare questions for the doctor.
User had loperamide at home and planned to take it before the bot advised checking first.
Mentioned as occasional blood in stool, used by the bot to frame the need for review.

output.summary: A user with ulcerative colitis on mesalamine described frequent, sudden urgency with occasional blood, saying they had been told this is normal and had seen a gastroenterologist only once. The bot explained step-up options, rectal mesalamine, a calprotectin test, ways to speed a referral, coping tips and caution about loperamide. The user said they felt ashamed at the start and now had a plan and could act.
